pr_title: fix(html)!: align html serving between dev and preview
pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing! -->

### Description

Supersedes https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/11289

Fixes https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/6596
Fixes https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/14690

**New behaviour:**

|                     | Before (dev)            | Before (preview)    | After (dev & preview)  |
|---------------------|-------------------------|---------------------|------------------------|
| `nested/index.html` | `nested/index.html`     | `nested/index.html` | `nested/index.html`    |
| `nested`            | `index.html`  (mpa 404) | `nested/index.html` | `index.html` (mpa 404) |
| `nested/`           | `nested/index.html`     | `nested/index.html` | `nested/index.html`    |
| `non-nested.html`   | `non-nested.html`       | `non-nested.html`   | `non-nested.html`      |
| `non-nested`        | `index.html` (mpa 404)  | `non-nested.html`   | `non-nested.html`      |
| `non-nested/`       | `index.html`  (mpa 404) | `non-nested.html`   | `index.html` (mpa 404) |

### Additional context

<!-- e.g. is there anything you'd like reviewers to focus on? -->
HTML files now also don't have `charset=utf-8` by default. I'm not really sure how to handle that and I've come to agree that it's also off that it's misaligned. Previously `charset=utf-8` is automatically added by `sirv` by default in preview, but not in dev.

Also removed `connect-history-api-fallback` and implement the fallback ourselves.

---

### What is the purpose of this pull request? <!-- (put an "X" next to an item) -->

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New Feature
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Other
pr_comments: _Run & review this pull request in [StackBlitz Codeflow](https://stackblitz.com/~/github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/14756)._

I think it would be better for @sapphi-red to review this one, but it looks good to me. I like moving away from `connect-history-api-fallback`, the new code looks easier to maintain than using the library.

Sapphi recommended to check with https://github.com/slorber/trailing-slash-guide, so here's the new comparison against it:

| Host | /file | /file/ | /file.html | /folder | /folder/ | /folder/index.html | /both | /both/ | /both.html | /both/index.html |
|------|-------|--------|------------|---------|----------|--------------------|-------|--------|------------|------------------|
| Vite | ✅     | ❌ (mpa 404) | ✅          | ❌ (mpa 404)  | ✅        | ✅                  | ✅     | ✅      | ✅          | ✅                |

The main difference is that we don't really do redirects if a trailing slash is needed/missing. And we don't do rewrites which can be dangerous when there's relative paths in the html. So for the most part I think this PR is good.

issue_context.title: Post middleware does not run for preview server
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

Looks like `vite dev` runs post middleware when requesting HTML pages (e.g., `index.html`) but `vite preview` does not. This seems to be because, requests for `index.html` are handled by Vite's asset middleware (`sirv`):

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/5b65bfdb4808660f63fcca15cbeea0fde1ae5b65/packages/vite/src/node/preview.ts#L169-L187

This discrepancy between `vite preview` and `vite dev` seems like it might be a bug, or at least undocumented/surprising, so posting here for visibility.

Furthermore, I noticed that `vite dev` does not run post middleware when handling JS, CSS, and static assets (e.g., images).

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vite-preview-middleware

### Steps to reproduce

- `vite dev`
  - Open https://stackblitz.com/edit/vite-preview-middleware, which runs `vite dev`.
  - Notice that both pre and post middleware runs for the `index.html` request, but only pre middleware runs for all other requests.
- `vite preview`
  - Open https://stackblitz.com/edit/vite-preview-middleware?startScript=build,preview, which runs `vite build` then `vite preview`.
  - Notice that _only_ pre middleware runs for all requests.


### System Info

(From StackBlitz terminal)

```shell
System:
  OS: Linux 5.0 undefined
  CPU: (8) x64 Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-9880H CPU @ 2.30GHz
  Memory: 0 Bytes / 0 Bytes
  Shell: 1.0 - /bin/jsh
Binaries:
  Node: 18.18.0 - /usr/local/bin/node
  Yarn: 1.22.19 - /usr/local/bin/yarn
  npm: 9.4.2 - /usr/local/bin/npm
  pnpm: 8.9.2 - /usr/local/bin/pnpm
npmPackages:
  vite: ^4.5.0 => 4.5.0
```


### Used Package Manager

npm

### Logs

#### `vite dev`:

```
Pre middleware: /
Post middleware: /index.html
Pre middleware: /@vite/client
Pre middleware: /main.js
Pre middleware: /node_modules/vite/dist/client/env.mjs
Pre middleware: /style.css
Pre middleware: /javascript.svg?import
Pre middleware: /vite.svg?import
Pre middleware: /counter.js
Pre middleware: /vite.svg
Pre middleware: /javascript.svg
Pre middleware: /vite.svg
```

#### `vite preview`:

```

Pre middleware: /assets/index-1fe36f1a.js
Pre middleware: /assets/index-9c1a2e68.css
Pre middleware: /vite.svg
Pre middleware: /assets/javascript-8dac5379.svg
```

IIUC this only happens if the base is without trailing slash (e.g. `/foo/bar`) and the prepended character doesn't have to be `.`.

We currently do pass the base with trailing slash, https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/7bd876c17c589e5f0bfc73fead8a358dd07420df/packages/vite/src/node/preview.ts#L193-L198

e.g. `/foo/bar/` in the assets playground, which stumped me how this is happening. And yeah it doesn't have to be a `.`. My initial workaround was prepending another slash, e.g. `req.url = '//index.html`, but that looks silly and harder to explain, so I only showed the `.` here.
